categories.main_business_segments: Affirm operates primarily as a next-generation payment network, offering point-of-sale financing and payment solutions. Its business is structured around three main segments: consumer point-of-sale payment solutions (including Pay-in-X, 0% APR, and interest-bearing installment loans), merchant commerce solutions (enabling merchants to offer Affirm at checkout and access analytics), and a consumer-focused app and marketplace. The company also issues the Affirm Card and provides high-yield savings accounts in partnership with banks.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Affirm’s platform is built on proprietary, cloud-first technology leveraging machine learning and artificial intelligence for transaction-level risk assessment and underwriting. The company’s systems aggregate and analyze data from over 343 million loans, enabling real-time credit decisions and fraud detection. Affirm invests heavily in in-house engineering, developing its own ledger and infrastructure to support rapid innovation, scalability, and integration with merchants via direct APIs.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Affirm serves a broad spectrum of consumers across the credit spectrum, focusing on those seeking transparent, flexible payment options. Its merchant customers range from small businesses to large enterprises and e-commerce platforms, spanning industries such as electronics, auto, fashion, general merchandise, home, sporting goods, and travel. Major end markets include U.S. retail, e-commerce, and increasingly, in-store and daily spending through the Affirm Card.
categories.geographic_coverage: Affirm’s primary market is the United States, with additional operations in Canada and the United Kingdom. The company is expanding internationally, with plans to enter Western Europe (including the Netherlands, France, and Germany) and Australia. As of June 30, 2025, the vast majority of business activity and revenue is generated in North America.
categories.supply_chain_position: Affirm operates at the downstream end of the financial services supply chain, directly interfacing with consumers at the point of sale and with merchants as a payment and commerce enablement partner. It acts as a facilitator and servicer of consumer loans, often purchasing loans originated by partner banks, and also provides servicing for third-party loan buyers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Affirm’s strategic priorities include expanding its consumer and merchant network, increasing transaction frequency and in-store usage (notably via the Affirm Card), and innovating new financial products and AI-powered personalization (e.g., AdaptAI). The company invests in technology to enhance underwriting, risk management, and user experience, and is focused on international expansion and deepening merchant partnerships.
categories.revenue_model: Affirm generates revenue primarily through merchant fees for facilitating sales and transactions, interest income from interest-bearing installment loans, card network revenue (a share of interchange fees from Affirm Card and virtual card transactions), gain on sale of loans, and servicing income from managing loan portfolios for third parties. Merchant fees are higher for 0% APR products, while most GMV is from interest-bearing loans.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Affirm competes with legacy credit and debit card issuers (e.g., Synchrony, JPMorgan Chase, Citibank, American Express), payment networks (Visa, MasterCard), mobile wallets (PayPal), and other pay-over-time providers (Block, Klarna), as well as proprietary merchant financing solutions. While many competitors are larger and more diversified, Affirm differentiates itself through technology, transparency, and a consumer-first approach.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, Affirm facilitated $36.7 billion in gross merchandise volume (GMV), up 38% year-over-year. Total revenue was $3.22 billion, a 39% increase from the prior year. The company achieved GAAP net income of $52.2 million in FY2025, following significant losses in prior years, and had approximately 23 million active consumers and 377,000 active merchants as of June 30, 2025.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Affirm’s core value proposition is built on transparency, simplicity, and consumer alignment—charging no late fees, no deferred or compounding interest, and providing clear, upfront terms. Its proprietary risk models enable higher approval rates and lower fraud compared to traditional credit, serving a wider range of consumers. For merchants, Affirm drives higher conversion, larger average order values, and provides actionable analytics, while consumers benefit from flexible, honest financial products.
